classes.desc: Minimal interval scheduler driven by a heap of next-run times.
classes.name: Scheduler

complexity: O(log j) per execution for j jobs
data_flow_ascii:
add_job(name, interval, func) -> heap of next-run times
run loop: pop due job -> func(name) -> log entry
         -> push back with next_run + interval
log -> execution table + per-job counts
description_sentence: Registers interval jobs on a heap scheduler, runs them for a fixed demo duration, and prints the execution log.
failure_note: A job that raises would propagate out of run(); demo jobs are side-effect-light counters, and the loop always exits at the deadline so it cannot hang.

functions.desc: Build a demo job function that counts its own executions.
functions.name: make_demo_job

functions.desc: Register `func` to run every `interval` seconds under `name`.
functions.name: Scheduler.add_job

functions.desc: Run scheduled jobs for `duration` seconds; return the log.
functions.name: Scheduler.run

functions.desc: Parse args, register demo jobs, run, and print the log.
functions.name: main

label: Task scheduler
output_shape: A timestamped execution table (time, job, result) plus per-job execution counts and a total.
pitch_sentence: A {topic} task scheduler in pure Python using a heap of next-run times, demonstrated by running real jobs on short intervals and printing the log.

qa.a: Yes; jobs reschedule themselves by next_run + interval, so a slow job does not drift its cadence.
qa.q: Do jobs keep their cadence if one runs long?

qa.a: No; everything runs on one thread, so jobs must be quick and non-blocking for the demo cadence to hold.
--duration sets the demo length and --jobs sets how many demo jobs register.

resume_bullet_template: Built a {topic} interval scheduler in Python (stdlib heapq) with drift-free rescheduling; demo registers jobs on sub-second intervals, runs them, and prints a timestamped execution log.
scaling_note: Single-threaded with O(log j) dispatch; suited to lightweight periodic jobs, not to thousands of concurrent or long-running tasks.
storage_note: In-memory only: the job heap and execution log exist for the run and are not persisted.
tradeoff_note: A heap loop is simple and precise for intervals but single-threaded, so blocking jobs would stall the whole schedule.
